name: North Carolina
agencyName: North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles

retake.waitBetweenAttempts: Retake on a later date; contact NCDMV for scheduling

gdl.nightCurfew: Level 1 and Level 2: unsupervised driving only 5 a.m.-9 p.m. (work, school, and emergency-service exceptions)
gdl.passengerLimits: Level 2: only one passenger under 21 who is not immediate family/household (with school-commute exception)

requiredDocuments: Proof of identity and date of birth (certified birth certificate or valid U.S. passport)
Two documents proving North Carolina residency
Proof of legal presence in the U.S. (if not a citizen)
Under 18: Driving Eligibility Certificate from your school
process.realIdNotes: North Carolina offers REAL ID-marked licenses. Bring one identity/DOB document, one SSN document, two residency documents, and proof of legal presence.
process.licenseFee: $6.50 per year (Class C; 8-year license about $52) as of July 1, 2024
process.visionStandard: At least 20/40 in at least one eye, with or without corrective lenses

facts.pointSuspensionThreshold: 12 points within 3 years may lead to suspension
facts.moveOverRule: Move over one lane, or slow down if unable, for stopped emergency and law-enforcement vehicles displaying flashing lights
facts.schoolZoneSpeed: As posted (commonly 20-35 mph when children are present)
namedLaws: Under-18 cell phone and texting ban

bacAdult.display: Impaired driving at an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more (or while under the influence of an impairing substance).

citation.label: Impaired driving

bacUnder21.display: Zero tolerance: a driver under 21 may not drive after consuming any alcohol or controlled substance; any alcohol concentration detected violates the statute.

citation.label: Driving by provisional licensee after consuming alcohol or drugs

bacCommercial.display: Commercial vehicle drivers commit impaired driving at an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more.

citation.label: Impaired driving in commercial vehicle

impliedConsentRefusal.display: Willful refusal of a chemical test triggers a 12-month civil revocation by the Division of Motor Vehicles; refusal is not itself a separate crime.

citation.label: Implied consent to chemical analysis; revocation for refusal

openContainerProhibited.display: It is unlawful under G.S. 20-138.7(a1) for any person to possess an open or unsealed alcoholic beverage container, or to consume alcohol, in the passenger area of a motor vehicle on a highway or its right-of-way; subsection (a) separately punishes a driver who does so while consuming alcohol or with alcohol remaining in the body.

citation.label: Transporting an open container of alcoholic beverage

duiFirstSuspensionDays.display: A first impaired-driving conviction requires mandatory revocation for one year (limited driving privilege possible).

citation.label: Mandatory revocation of license by Division

conditions.detail: rural interstate highways where 70 mph is posted

ruralInterstateMaxMph.display: 55 mph statewide outside municipalities; the Department of Transportation may raise limits to a maximum of 70 mph where posted, and 70 mph is posted on rural interstates.

citation.label: Speed restrictions

conditions.detail: urban interstate highways where 70 mph is posted

urbanInterstateMaxMph.display: Maximum posted speed limit on urban interstates is 70 mph (statutory ceiling of 70 mph under G.S. 20-141(d)(2)).

citation.label: IIHS maximum posted speed limits by state (July 2026)
citation.citation: IIHS, Maximum posted speed limits (North Carolina: 70 mph rural and urban interstates)

conditions.detail: inside municipal corporate limits, unless a different limit is posted

residentialDefaultMph.display: Unless otherwise posted, 35 mph inside municipal corporate limits and 55 mph outside municipal corporate limits.

citation.label: Speed restrictions

state.reason: North Carolina sets no statewide school-zone speed limit. Under G.S. 20-141.1 local authorities and the Department of Transportation may set school-zone limits, which may not be below 20 mph, and they are enforceable only while posted and while children are going to or leaving school during opening or closing hours.

schoolZoneMph.display: No single statewide school-zone speed limit: locally established limits (never below 20 mph) apply only when posted and when school is opening or closing.

citation.label: Speed limits in school zones

basicSpeedLaw.display: No person shall drive at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the conditions then existing.

citation.label: Speed restrictions

rightTurnOnRed.display: After coming to a complete stop at a steady red circular light, a driver may turn right unless prohibited by an appropriate sign.

citation.label: Vehicle control signs and signals

leftTurnOnRedFromOneWay.display: G.S. 20-158(b)(2)a authorizes only a right turn after stopping at a steady red light; no left turn on red from a one-way street is authorized.

citation.label: Vehicle control signs and signals

conditions.detail: driver and front-seat occupants, and all occupants under 16

seatBeltEnforcement.display: Primary enforcement for the driver, front-seat occupants and occupants under 16; a rear-seat belt violation by an occupant 16 or older may not be the sole basis for a stop.

citation.label: Seat belt use required

handheldPhone.display: No general handheld ban: drivers under 18 may not use a mobile telephone while driving (limited emergency and parent-call exceptions).

citation.label: Unlawful use of mobile telephone by persons under 18

texting.display: No driver may manually enter or read text-based communication (texts, e-mail) while operating a vehicle on a public street or highway.

citation.label: Unlawful use of mobile telephone for text messaging or electronic mail

moveOver.display: Approaching a stopped emergency or public service vehicle displaying flashing lights, a driver must move into a lane not adjacent when possible on a multi-lane road, otherwise slow down and proceed with caution.

citation.label: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 20-157(f) as rewritten by S.L. 2022-68, s. 6.(a) (s. 6.(b): effective August 1, 2022)
citation.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 20-157(f); 2022 N.C. Sess. Laws 68, s. 6

headlightsRequired.display: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise, whenever windshield wipers are in continuous use because of precipitation, and whenever visibility is under 500 feet.

citation.label: Required lighting equipment of vehicles

parkFtFromHydrant.display: No parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

citation.label: Parking in front of private driveway, fire hydrant, private road or alley

state.reason: North Carolina has no statewide statutory parking setback from a crosswalk; G.S. 20-162 lists only driveways, hydrants, private roads and alleys, and G.S. 20-169 leaves parking regulation on non-State-maintained streets to local ordinance.

parkFtFromCrosswalk.display: No statewide crosswalk parking setback; crosswalk parking restrictions are set by local ordinance or posted signs.

citation.label: Parking in front of private driveway, fire hydrant, private road or alley

state.reason: North Carolina has no statewide statutory parking setback from a stop sign; G.S. 20-162 does not address stop signs and local authorities regulate parking under G.S. 20-169.

parkFtFromStopSign.display: No statewide stop-sign parking setback; such restrictions come from local ordinance or posted signs.

citation.label: Parking in front of private driveway, fire hydrant, private road or alley

state.reason: North Carolina has no statewide statutory parking setback from a railroad crossing; G.S. 20-162 does not address railroad crossings and local authorities regulate parking under G.S. 20-169.

parkFtFromRailroad.display: No statewide railroad-crossing parking setback; such restrictions come from local ordinance or posted signs.

citation.label: Parking in front of private driveway, fire hydrant, private road or alley

pointSystem.display: The Division of Motor Vehicles assigns driver license points for moving violations and may suspend a license on point accumulation.

citation.label: Authority of Division to suspend license

pointSuspension.display: The Division may suspend a license when a driver accumulates 12 points within any three-year period (8 points within three years after reinstatement).

citation.label: Authority of Division to suspend license

permitMinAgeMonths.display: A limited learner permit (Level 1) may be issued at 15 years of age after driver education and a written test.

citation.label: Issuance of limited learner's permit and provisional drivers license to person who is less than 18 years old

permitHoldingMonths.display: The limited learner permit must be held at least nine months before a limited provisional license (Level 2) may be issued at 16.

citation.label: Issuance of limited learner's permit and provisional drivers license to person who is less than 18 years old

supervisedHoursTotal.display: A driving log showing a minimum of 60 hours of supervised driving is required for the limited provisional license; no more than 10 hours per week may be counted.

citation.label: Issuance of limited learner's permit and provisional drivers license to person who is less than 18 years old

supervisedHoursNight.display: At least 10 of the 60 logged supervised hours must be during nighttime hours.

citation.label: Issuance of limited learner's permit and provisional drivers license to person who is less than 18 years old

gdlNightCurfew.display: A limited provisional (Level 2) licensee may drive unsupervised only from 5:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m., with exceptions for driving directly to or from work or volunteer emergency service.

citation.label: Issuance of limited learner's permit and provisional drivers license to person who is less than 18 years old

gdlPassengerPhase1.display: When driving unsupervised, a limited provisional licensee may carry no more than one passenger under 21; immediate family and household members are exempt (but if such a family passenger under 21 is aboard, no other passengers under 21 are allowed).

citation.label: Issuance of limited learner's permit and provisional drivers license to person who is less than 18 years old

minLiability.display: Minimum motor vehicle liability limits are $50,000 per person / $100,000 per accident for bodily injury and $50,000 for property damage (raised by S.L. 2023-133 for policies issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2025).

citation.label: S.L. 2023-133, Part XII, s. 12.(i) (raising G.S. 20-279.21(b)(2) limits)

crashReportThresholdUsd.display: A crash must be reported when it results in death or injury, or apparent property damage of at least $1,000.

citation.label: Duty to report accidents

verifyNote: Official NCDMV sources confirm the 25-question road-rules test and $25.50 Level 1 fee, but the separate road-sign test's exact 8-question/6-correct format was not located in a current official source.
